newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for June 23.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for June 23.

text.p: All Mexican ports were open on Monday to large ships, the Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT) said in its 1500 local/2000 GMT daily meteorological report.
Key cargo port Lazaro Cardenas was closed to smaller fishing and tourism ships amid winds of 12.5 miles (20 km) per hour and slight waves.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Pacific Coast, Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean.
Clear skies and hot temperatures with maximum winds 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 16 miles per hour) and waves three to five feet high.

Tropical winds along the southern coast showering rains along Colima, Michoacan, Oaxaca, Guerrero and Chiapas. New storms off the coast causing winds of 20 to 30 knots (38 to 56 km/22 to 32 miles per hour) and waves eight to 12 feet high.
Strong rains along Veracruz and Tamaulipas coasts. Winds in the region from 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 km/16 to 22 miles per hour).
Hot and partly cloudy with light rains in Quintana Roo and regional winds about 10 to 15 knots, with waves four to six feet high.
Light rains along Nicaragua, Panama and Costa Rica.
